title: AI-Driven Healthcare: A Review on Ensuring Fairness and Mitigating Bias

bias_targets.methodology: Reviewing literature on healthcare algorithms to evaluate performance disparities, such as lower diagnostic accuracy for darker skin tones in dermatology AI and resource allocation algorithms that disproportionately favor white patients over sicker black patients.

Using theoretical case studies (e.g., organ allocation and heart disease prediction) and reviewing causal modeling techniques to evaluate differences in prediction accuracy, true positive rates, and resource approval rates between male and female patients using metrics like Statistical Parity and Equalized Odds.

Discussing the evaluation of predictive models that use proxies like healthcare costs or private insurance status, which implicitly disadvantage specific socioeconomic groups, and assessing them through the lens of algorithmic fairness metrics and causal modeling.

Highlighting evaluation disparities in AI diagnostic tools (e.g., depression diagnostics) that are trained predominantly on English-speaking, Western populations, leading to potential misdiagnoses when applied to non-Western and non-English-speaking patients.
